title: Trombonist Big Chief Russell Moore, picked up in Monroe
summary: Harris tells how the band found Russell Moore in Monroe, why he left in Tallahassee, and later meetings.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Oh, excuse me for interrupting. I was going to ask some more about this trombone player, Big Chief, Russell Moore. Russell Moore, yeah. Because I met him in New York once. I thought he came from, say, the Indian territory or something like that. Oklahoma.

Oklahoma. He was on a recreation. See, when we was in Tallahassee, I think it was Tallahassee, Florida, he got a letter to report back because his parents had died and had some property to sell or something like that. Well, he had to leave the band and go back to Oklahoma on the reservation.
He was part Indian then, wasn't he? Yes. Did he come right from the reservation? No.
When we got him, I think he just said... I mean, his folks and all.
Yeah, his folks was all from the reservation. They were almost on the reservation. Some of those Indians inherited the oil and everything else, I think.
Yeah, well, he had a property, a lot of property they had to sell over there, so he had to leave the band. He left us in Tallahassee, Florida.
Had he been around in New Orleans long or did you work with him mostly traveling around

outside? No, I tell you, we picked him up in Monroe, Louisiana. He was traveling with a little band out of Monroe. And the Celestan band was playing at night. They had a club over there on De Hennessy Street, I think it is. He called it the Savoy. Well, this was an opening night that night and we had the job to open it up. That's the time when Anderson was making all those high notes and they wanted to write the ripplet. He was the first to make all those high notes on the trumpets, you know? And that's when we met this boy. We met, he was sitting on the hotel steps. So, Father Celestan said, who is this fellow sitting over there? I said, I heard him playing trombone on the day. He said he played good. So, we called him over to a cafe where we were and asked him to join the band. He said, yeah, he joined the band that night. So, that's when we had two trombones. Bill Matthews, who was at the paddock with Octave Crosby. Yeah. Well, I think it was after I left Celestan there and I went with Octave Crosby at the Budweiser. At the tuxedo club. And from the tuxedo club I went to the Budweiser with Artie. Then I went with Smiling Joe out at the hit Gendlin's famous door on Wednesday.

The last time I saw the big chief, as they call him, Moore, he was at the famous door. He stopped in to see some of the musicians. I think Santa Picora and others he knew. And I was surprised they all knew him. I'd never known he'd been down this part of the country at that time.

He looked all over town for me. And he found me at the duteron. I was sitting at the boy Drake and I was somebody packing on the show, you know. He was down there with Louis Armstrong. You remember the town of Louis Camp? Yeah, I know. Well, he came down to the duteron. He shook my hand. He played piano too. He did?
I know. He played a lot of piano. I know he traveled with Sidney Bechet once about ten years ago exactly. I guess I heard him with Sidney in Chicago.
